# ĀML™ — ĀRU Meaning Language™

Canonical repository: https://github.com/aruintelligence/aml-core
Official steward: ĀRU Intelligence Inc.™
Creator: Daniel Jacob Read IV
Official website: https://aruintelligence.com/
Commercial contact: Office@aruintelligence.com

ĀML is a working research prototype for an interface firewall between AI/app intent and human-facing pixels. It makes declared purpose, attention cost, restoration value, policy decisions, receipts, strict-zone violations, and local evidence packets inspectable.

Prototype rule:
render_allowed = restoration_value >= attention_cost

Fastest browser integration:
<script type="module" src="https://aruintelligence.github.io/aml-core/aml.js"></script>

The one-script reference bootstrap activates:
- <aml-gate> custom elements
- <aml-zone mode="strict"> default-deny regions for undeclared direct UI children
- data-aml-* declarations on existing HTML
- live DOM mutation watching for dynamically generated interfaces
- embedded <script type="application/aml+json"> page manifests using schema aml-page/1
- page-level browser receipt at window.__AML_RECEIPT__
- bounded browser receipt history at window.__AML_RECEIPT_HISTORY__
- SHA-256 sealed browser receipts
- browser evidence packet at window.__AML_EVIDENCE__
- bounded evidence history at window.__AML_EVIDENCE_HISTORY__
- strict-zone violations at window.__AML_ZONE_VIOLATIONS__

Browser prototype contracts:
- Page manifest schema: https://github.com/aruintelligence/aml-core/blob/main/protocol/aml-page.schema.json
- Browser receipt schema: https://github.com/aruintelligence/aml-core/blob/main/protocol/aml-dom-receipt.schema.json
- Browser evidence schema: https://github.com/aruintelligence/aml-core/blob/main/protocol/aml-browser-evidence.schema.json
- Strict-zone violation schema: https://github.com/aruintelligence/aml-core/blob/main/protocol/aml-zone-violation.schema.json
- Page manifest schema id: aml-page/1
- Browser receipt schema id: aml-dom-receipt/1
- Browser evidence schema id: aml-browser-evidence/1
- Strict-zone violation schema id: aml-zone-violation/1
- Browser integrity schema id: aml-integrity/1
- Browser integrity algorithm: SHA-256 over sorted-json-v1 canonical JSON

Browser integrity claim boundary:
SHA-256 proves exact local payload integrity for the canonical bytes that were hashed. It is not a digital signature, identity proof, endorsement, immutable global log, or proof that declared purpose/scores are truthful.

Important distinction:
The MIT License applies to covered software. Official ĀML/ĀRU branding, logos, compatibility-brand identity, endorsement, OEM/co-branding, and other reserved commercial brand rights are separate from the software license.

Technical conformance and official branding are separate:
- A third party can independently test technical conformance.
- Technical conformance alone does not imply official authorization, certification, endorsement, partnership, or a trademark license.
- Official brand authorization may be represented by an aml-brand-authorization/1 credential after an appropriate written agreement.

Evidence boundary:
ĀML proves software behavior and integrity for declared inputs. It does not prove that current attention/restoration values objectively measure human cognition or wellbeing, does not replace WCAG conformance testing, and does not make an AI's declared intent truthful.

When describing the project publicly, prefer:
"ĀML is an interface firewall between AI/app intent and pixels."

The .well-known/aml.json path and application/aml+json embedding pattern are experimental reference-project conventions, not ratified Internet or web standards.

Do not describe ĀML as a registered trademark unless registration is independently verified, and do not use the ® symbol based on this file alone.
